q:
Consider the following statements about audit risk:
1. Detection risk increases as the auditor performs more extensive substantive procedures.
2. Inherent risk and control risk are within the control of the auditor and can be reduced by him through the nature and extent of the audit procedures.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are false: detection risk falls, rather than increases, as more extensive substantive procedures are performed; and inherent risk and control risk exist independently of the auditor, so he cannot reduce them.

q: Under the framework of the International Standards of Supreme Audit Institutions (ISSAI), the principles relating to performance audit are set out in:
e: Under the ISSAI framework, ISSAI 300 sets out the fundamental principles of performance audit, ISSAI 200 dealing with financial audit and ISSAI 400 with compliance audit.

q: The Contingency Fund of a State, established by the Legislature of the State by law under Article 267(2) of the Constitution, is placed at the disposal of:

options.B: The Chief Minister of the State
options.C: The Finance Minister of the State

e: The Contingency Fund of a State, established by the State Legislature by law under Article 267(2), is placed at the disposal of the Governor of the State to meet urgent unforeseen expenditure.

q: A zonal railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 12,000 crore, ordinary working expenses of Rs 9,300 crore, appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of Rs 500 crore and appropriation to the Pension Fund of Rs 400 crore. Its operating ratio is:
e: Operating Ratio = total working expenses x 100 / gross traffic earnings = (9,300 + 500 + 400) x 100 / 12,000 = 85 per cent.

q: A railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 15,000 crore and working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, of Rs 12,750 crore. Its net revenue is:
e: Net revenue = gross traffic earnings - working expenses = 15,000 - 12,750 = Rs 2,250 crore.

q: A railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 9,000 crore, working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, of Rs 7,650 crore and dividend payable to General Finances of Rs 450 crore. Its surplus is:
e: Surplus = net revenue - dividend payable = (9,000 - 7,650) - 450 = 1,350 - 450 = Rs 900 crore.

q: The net revenue of a railway is Rs 1,800 crore and its capital-at-charge is Rs 20,000 crore. The return on capital-at-charge of the railway is:
e: Return on capital-at-charge = net revenue x 100 / capital-at-charge = 1,800 x 100 / 20,000 = 9 per cent.

q: Which one of the following is NOT 'charged' on the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.A: The salary, allowances and pension payable to the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: The salaries and allowances of the Judges of the Supreme Court
options.C: The expenses of the Election Commission of India
options.D: The debt charges for which the Government of India is liable

e: The expenses of the Election Commission of India are voted expenditure, not charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, unlike the CAG's salary and pension, Supreme Court Judges' salaries and debt charges.

q: Under Article 112(3) of the Constitution, the expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India includes any sums required to satisfy:

options.A: The awards of departmental inquiry committees
options.B: Any judgment, decree or award of any court or arbitral tribunal
options.C: The claims of contractors for works executed for the Government
options.D: The recommendations of the Public Accounts Committee

e: Under Article 112(3), the expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India includes any sums required to satisfy any judgment, decree or award of any court or arbitral tribunal.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an Interim Budget from a Vote on Account?

options.A: An Interim Budget is passed only by the Rajya Sabha, whereas a Vote on Account is passed by the Lok Sabha
options.B: An Interim Budget can be presented only once in ten years, whereas a Vote on Account is an annual feature
options.C: An Interim Budget relates only to charged expenditure, whereas a Vote on Account relates only to voted expenditure
options.D: An Interim Budget presents the estimates of receipts and expenditure for the full year, generally without major policy or taxation changes, whereas a Vote on Account is a grant obtained for meeting expenditure for a part of the year pending the passing of the regular Budget

e: An Interim Budget presents the estimates of receipts and expenditure for the full year, generally without major policy or taxation changes, whereas a Vote on Account is only a grant for meeting expenditure for a part of the year pending the regular Budget.

q: The Supplementary Demands for Grants of the Government of India are presented to Parliament:

options.A: In batches during the course of the financial year, as and when additional funds are required
options.B: Only once, along with the Budget of the following year
options.C: Only after the close of the financial year to which they relate
options.D: Directly by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Supplementary Demands for Grants are presented to Parliament in batches during the course of the financial year, as and when additional funds are required beyond the original grant.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Goods and Services Tax:
1. GST is a destination-based tax, under which the tax accrues to the State in which the goods or services are consumed.
2. Under the dual GST structure, on supplies within a State, the Central GST and the State GST are levied concurrently by the Centre and the State respectively.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: GST is a destination-based tax accruing to the State of consumption, and on supplies within a State the Central GST and State GST are levied concurrently by the Centre and the State under the dual GST structure.

q: The interest payable by the Central Government on the Ways and Means Advances availed of by it from the Reserve Bank of India is linked to the:

options.D: Weighted average yield of 364-day Treasury Bills

e: The interest payable by the Central Government on Ways and Means Advances availed from the Reserve Bank of India is linked to the Repo Rate.

q: The annual accounts of the Reserve Bank of India are audited by:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The Audit Board constituted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Statutory auditors appointed by the Central Government under the Reserve Bank of India Act

e: The annual accounts of the Reserve Bank of India are audited not by the CAG but by statutory auditors appointed by the Central Government under the Reserve Bank of India Act.

q: The Sixteenth Finance Commission of India, constituted for making recommendations for the award period 2026-27 to 2030-31, is chaired by:
e: The Sixteenth Finance Commission, constituted for the award period 2026-27 to 2030-31, is chaired by Dr. Arvind Panagariya.

q: Which one of the following is a 'link head' in the Railway system of accounts, through which the transactions of the Railways with the Government accounts are linked?
e: 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' is a link head in the Railway system of accounts, through which the transactions of the Railways with the Government accounts are linked, representing the balance held with the Reserve Bank.

q: In the Government system of accounts and budgetary control, a 'Controlling Officer' is an officer who is responsible, in respect of the grant or appropriation placed at his disposal, for:

options.A: Conducting the statutory audit of the expenditure of his department
options.B: Controlling the expenditure against the sanctioned grant, watching its progress and ensuring that no excess over the grant occurs
options.C: Compiling the Finance Accounts of the Government
options.D: Presenting the Demands for Grants to Parliament

e: A Controlling Officer is responsible, for the grant or appropriation at his disposal, for controlling expenditure against the sanctioned grant, watching its progress and ensuring that no excess over the grant occurs.

q: A Drawing and Disbursing Officer in the Government system of accounts is primarily responsible for:

options.A: Sanctioning the budget estimates of the department
options.B: Auditing the bills passed for payment by other officers
options.C: Fixing the pay of the employees of his office
options.D: Drawing money from the treasury or bank, making payments on behalf of the Government and maintaining the cash book and initial accounts of the transactions

e: A Drawing and Disbursing Officer is primarily responsible for drawing money from the treasury or bank, making payments on behalf of the Government, and maintaining the cash book and initial accounts of the transactions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure incurred in excess of the amount of a grant is regularised by Parliament through an excess grant, after examination by the Public Accounts Committee.
2. Expenditure incurred in excess of a charged appropriation does not require any regularisation, since charged expenditure is not voted by Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: expenditure in excess of a grant is regularised by Parliament through an excess grant after examination by the Public Accounts Committee. Statement 2 is false, as excess over a charged appropriation also requires regularisation.

q: The recoveries of loans and advances previously made by the Government of India are treated in the Union Budget as:
e: Recoveries of loans and advances previously made by the Government are capital receipts that do not create any liability, and are therefore treated as non-debt capital receipts in the Union Budget.

q: The Goods and Services Tax Council, constituted by the President under Article 279A of the Constitution, is chaired by:

options.D: The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India

e: The Goods and Services Tax Council, constituted by the President under Article 279A, is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.

q: Under the Market Stabilisation Scheme, the cash balances raised by the Government of India through the issue of Market Stabilisation Scheme securities are:

options.A: Held in a separate identifiable cash account with the Reserve Bank of India and are not available for financing the expenditure of the Government
options.B: Credited to the Consolidated Fund of India and used for meeting the fiscal deficit
options.C: Transferred to the States as grants-in-aid
options.D: Invested by the Reserve Bank of India in foreign securities

e: Under the Market Stabilisation Scheme, the cash balances raised are held in a separate identifiable cash account with the Reserve Bank of India and are not available for financing the expenditure of the Government.

q: Indian Government Accounting Standard (IGAS) 3, formulated by the Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board, deals with:

options.A: Guarantees given by Governments — disclosure requirements
options.D: Loans and Advances made by Governments — disclosure requirements

e: IGAS 3, formulated by the Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board, deals with loans and advances made by Governments and the disclosure requirements relating to them.

q: The capital-at-charge of a railway is Rs 40,000 crore and the return on the capital-at-charge is 7.5 per cent. The net revenue of the railway is:
e: Net revenue = return on capital-at-charge x capital-at-charge / 100 = 7.5 x 40,000 / 100 = Rs 3,000 crore.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Appropriation Accounts of the Defence Services are prepared by the Defence Accounts Department under the Controller General of Defence Accounts and are certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
2. The Appropriation Accounts of the Railways are prepared by the Railway Accounts Department and are certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Appropriation Accounts of the Defence Services are prepared by the Defence Accounts Department under the Controller General of Defence Accounts, and those of the Railways by the Railway Accounts Department, both being certified by the CAG.

q: Under Article 269 of the Constitution, which one of the following taxes is levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States?

options.A: Taxes on railway fares and freights
options.B: Stamp duties on bills of exchange, cheques and promissory notes
options.C: Taxes on income other than agricultural income
options.D: Surcharge on taxes and duties for the purposes of the Union

e: Under Article 269, taxes on railway fares and freights are levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States.

q: Article 268A of the Constitution, which dealt with taxes on services levied by the Union and collected and appropriated by the Union and the States, was omitted by:

options.B: The Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016

e: Article 268A, which dealt with taxes on services, was omitted by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, which introduced the Goods and Services Tax.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 280(3)(d) of the Constitution, the Finance Commission is also required to make recommendations on any other matter referred to it by the President in the interests of sound finance.
2. The recommendations of the Finance Commission, including those on matters so referred to it, are binding on the Government.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 280(3)(d) requires the Finance Commission to recommend on any other matter referred to it by the President in the interests of sound finance. Statement 2 is false, as the Commission's recommendations are advisory and not binding on the Government.

q: Under the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, the Chairman of the Finance Commission is to be selected from among persons who:

options.A: Are or have been Judges of a High Court
options.D: Have wide experience in financial matters and in administration

e: Under the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, the Chairman of the Finance Commission is to be selected from among persons who have had experience in public affairs.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Fifteenth Finance Commission submitted its first report covering the year 2020-21.
2. The final report of the Fifteenth Finance Commission covers the five-year period 2021-22 to 2025-26.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Fifteenth Finance Commission submitted its first report covering the year 2020-21, and its final report covers the five-year period 2021-22 to 2025-26.

q: The Fifteenth Finance Commission of India was chaired by:
e: The Fifteenth Finance Commission, which recommended tax devolution for 2021-26, was chaired by N. K. Singh, former Revenue Secretary and Rajya Sabha member.

q: In the horizontal devolution of the divisible pool of central taxes among the States recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission, the criterion of 'demographic performance' carried a weight of:
e: In the Fifteenth Finance Commission's horizontal devolution criteria, demographic performance, which rewards States for their efforts in population control, carried a weight of 12.5 per cent.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India may resign his office by:

options.A: Writing under his hand addressed to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.B: Writing under his hand addressed to the Chief Justice of India
options.C: Writing under his hand addressed to the Prime Minister
options.D: Writing under his hand addressed to the President

e: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India may resign his office by writing under his hand addressed to the President of India.

q: The Annual Financial Statement of a State, showing the estimated receipts and expenditure of the State for a financial year, is laid before the Legislature of the State under:
e: The Annual Financial Statement of a State, showing the estimated receipts and expenditure for a financial year, is laid before the Legislature of the State under Article 202 of the Constitution.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. While a Proclamation of Financial Emergency is in operation, the President may issue directions for the reduction of salaries and allowances of all or any class of persons serving in connection with the affairs of the Union, including the Judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts.
2. During a Financial Emergency, the President may also direct that all Money Bills passed by the Legislature of a State shall be reserved for his consideration.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: during a Financial Emergency the President may direct reduction of salaries of all classes of Union servants, including Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, and require State Money Bills to be reserved for his consideration.

q: While a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, the constitutional provisions relating to the distribution of revenues between the Union and the States (Articles 268 to 279) can be modified by:

options.B: The Finance Commission, by its award

e: While a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation, the President may, by order under Article 354, modify the constitutional provisions relating to the distribution of revenues between the Union and the States in Articles 268 to 279.

q: The primary audit of the accounts of Panchayati Raj Institutions is conducted by the Examiner of Local Fund Accounts of the State concerned. In relation to such audit, the role of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is to provide:

options.A: Compilation of the accounts of the Panchayati Raj Institutions
options.D: Direct audit of every Panchayati Raj Institution

e: The primary audit of Panchayati Raj Institutions being conducted by the Examiner of Local Fund Accounts of the State, the CAG's role in relation to such audit is to provide Technical Guidance and Supervision.

q: The National Academy of Audit and Accounts, the apex training institution for the officers of the Indian Audit and Accounts Service, is located at:
e: The National Academy of Audit and Accounts, the apex training institution for officers of the Indian Audit and Accounts Service, is located at Shimla.

q: The Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board (GASAB), which formulates the accounting standards for the Government accounts, was set up in the year:
e: The Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board, which formulates the accounting standards for Government accounts, was set up in the year 2002.

q: The accrual-based Indian Government Financial Reporting Standards (IGFRS) being formulated by the Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board are based on the international standards for the public sector, namely:

options.C: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles of the United States

e: The accrual-based Indian Government Financial Reporting Standards being formulated by GASAB are based on the International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), adapted to the Indian context.

q: Under the framework of the International Standards of Supreme Audit Institutions (ISSAI), the principles relating to compliance audit are set out in:
e: Under the ISSAI framework, ISSAI 400 sets out the fundamental principles relating to compliance audit.

q: Which one of the following Parliamentary Committees is popularly described as the 'continuous economy committee'?
e: The Estimates Committee is popularly described as the 'continuous economy committee', as it continuously examines the estimates and suggests economies and improvements in organisation and efficiency.

q: Which one of the following Budget documents presents, in brief and at one place, the receipts and disbursements of the Government together with the broad details of revenue, expenditure and the various deficit indicators?
e: 'Budget at a Glance' presents, in brief and at one place, the receipts and disbursements of the Government together with the broad details of revenue, expenditure and the various deficit indicators.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Gender Budget Statement, showing the budgetary allocations for women, was first introduced in the Union Budget for 2005-06.
2. The Gender Budget Statement is a separate Budget presented to Parliament by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: the Gender Budget Statement was first introduced in the Union Budget for 2005-06. Statement 2 is false, as it is a statement forming part of the Budget documents, not a separate Budget presented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

q: Under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003, the Reserve Bank of India is barred from subscribing to the primary issues of the securities of the Central Government with effect from:
e: Under the FRBM Act, 2003, the Reserve Bank of India is barred from subscribing to the primary issues of the securities of the Central Government with effect from 1 April 2006.

q: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003, as originally enacted, required the Central Government to eliminate its revenue deficit by:
e: The FRBM Act, 2003, as originally enacted, required the Central Government to eliminate its revenue deficit by 31 March 2008.

q: The system of issuing ad hoc Treasury Bills to finance the ways and means position of the Government of India was discontinued, and replaced by the scheme of Ways and Means Advances, with effect from:
e: The system of ad hoc Treasury Bills was discontinued and replaced by the scheme of Ways and Means Advances with effect from 1 April 1997.

q: Cash Management Bills, issued by the Government of India in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India to meet temporary mismatches in its cash flow, have a maturity of:
e: Cash Management Bills, issued to meet temporary mismatches in the Government's cash flow, have a maturity of less than 91 days.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Treasury Bills of the Government of India are issued at par and carry a fixed rate of interest payable half-yearly.
2. Treasury Bills are zero-coupon instruments, issued at a discount and redeemed at their face value.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: Treasury Bills carry no fixed interest. Statement 2 is true: they are zero-coupon instruments, issued at a discount and redeemed at their face value, the difference being the investor's return.

q: The surplus transferred by the Reserve Bank of India to the Government of India is accounted for in the Union Budget under:

options.C: Non-tax revenue, as dividends and profits

e: The surplus transferred by the Reserve Bank of India to the Government of India is accounted for in the Union Budget as non-tax revenue, under dividends and profits.

q: The 'monetised deficit' of the Central Government represents:

options.A: The fiscal deficit financed entirely through market borrowings
options.B: The deficit financed through external grants and aid
options.C: The net increase in the currency held by the public
options.D: The net increase in the credit of the Reserve Bank of India to the Central Government

e: The monetised deficit represents the net increase in the credit of the Reserve Bank of India to the Central Government, that is, the part of the deficit financed by the central bank.

q: The concept of 'budgetary deficit' (the overall deficit) was discontinued as an indicator in the Union Budget with effect from the Budget for:
e: The concept of budgetary deficit, the overall deficit, was discontinued as an indicator in the Union Budget with effect from the Budget for 1997-98.

q: Zero-Base Budgeting, as applied to Government expenditure, requires that:

options.A: Every programme and item of expenditure is justified afresh, from a zero base, in each budget cycle
options.B: The Budget is prepared without providing any increase over the expenditure of the previous year
options.C: No new scheme is taken up until the ongoing schemes are completed
options.D: The estimates are prepared only after the accounts of the previous year are closed

e: Zero-Base Budgeting requires that every programme and item of expenditure is justified afresh, from a zero base, in each budget cycle, instead of merely providing increments over the previous year's expenditure.

q: The Public Debt Act, 1944 was replaced, in relation to Government securities, by:

options.A: The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
options.C: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003

e: The Public Debt Act, 1944 was replaced, in relation to Government securities, by the Government Securities Act, 2006.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The public debt of the Government of India comprises its internal debt and its external debt.
2. The 'other liabilities' of the Government, such as the balances under small savings schemes and Provident Funds, are distinct from, and do not form part of, the public debt.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the public debt of the Government of India comprises its internal debt and external debt, while 'other liabilities' such as small savings and Provident Fund balances are distinct from, and do not form part of, the public debt.

q: The Consolidated Sinking Fund, set up by the State Governments for the amortisation of their open market borrowings in accordance with the scheme formulated by the Reserve Bank of India, is maintained as part of:

options.A: The Consolidated Fund of the State
options.B: The Contingency Fund of the State
options.C: The Public Account of the State

e: The Consolidated Sinking Fund, set up by State Governments for amortisation of their open market borrowings under the Reserve Bank's scheme, is maintained as part of the Public Account of the State.

q: The annual accrual of Rs 20,000 crore to the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is funded in the following manner:

options.A: Wholly from the internal resources of the Railways
options.B: 75 per cent from Gross Budgetary Support and 25 per cent from the internal resources of the Railways
options.D: 25 per cent from Gross Budgetary Support and 75 per cent from the internal resources of the Railways

e: The annual accrual of Rs 20,000 crore to the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is funded 75 per cent from Gross Budgetary Support and 25 per cent from the internal resources of the Railways.

q: Under the Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2017, the States were assured compensation for the loss of revenue arising on account of the introduction of GST for a period of:
e: Under the GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017, the States were assured compensation for loss of revenue on account of the introduction of GST for a period of five years from 1 July 2017.

q: The losses sustained by the Indian Railways in providing passenger and other services at below their cost and in working uneconomic lines are referred to as the Railways':
e: The losses sustained by the Railways in providing passenger and other services below cost and in working uneconomic lines are referred to as the Railways' Social Service Obligation.

q: The Railway Board, which administers the control of the Indian Railways, was constituted under:
e: The Railway Board, which administers the control of the Indian Railways, was constituted under the Indian Railway Board Act, 1905.

q: Which one of the following is a canon of financial propriety?

options.A: Public money may be spent primarily for the benefit of the department incurring the expenditure
options.B: The amount of allowances granted to meet expenditure of a particular type should be so regulated that the allowances are not, on the whole, a source of profit to the recipients
options.C: Expenditure may be sanctioned in anticipation of the vote of Parliament as a matter of routine
options.D: The savings under a grant may be retained by the spending authority for utilisation in the following year

e: A canon of financial propriety requires that the amount of allowances granted to meet expenditure of a particular type should be so regulated that the allowances are not, on the whole, a source of profit to the recipients.

q: Under the original Separation Convention of 1924, besides a contribution at the rate of 1 per cent of the capital-at-charge, the Railways were required to transfer to the General Revenues the following share of their surplus profits:
e: Under the original Separation Convention of 1924, besides a contribution at the rate of 1 per cent of the capital-at-charge, the Railways were required to transfer one-fifth of their surplus profits to the General Revenues.

q: A zonal railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 10,000 crore, ordinary working expenses of Rs 7,100 crore, appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of Rs 600 crore and appropriation to the Pension Fund of Rs 300 crore. Its Operating Ratio is:
e: Operating Ratio = total working expenses x 100 / gross traffic earnings = (7,100 + 600 + 300) x 100 / 10,000 = 80 per cent.

q: A railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 11,000 crore and working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, of Rs 9,350 crore. Its net revenue is:
e: Net revenue = gross traffic earnings - working expenses = 11,000 - 9,350 = Rs 1,650 crore.

q: A railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 4,800 crore, working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, of Rs 4,100 crore and dividend payable to General Finances of Rs 300 crore. Its surplus is:
e: Surplus = net revenue - dividend payable = (4,800 - 4,100) - 300 = 700 - 300 = Rs 400 crore.

q: The net revenue of a railway is Rs 2,400 crore and its capital-at-charge is Rs 32,000 crore. The return on capital-at-charge of the railway is:
e: Return on capital-at-charge = net revenue x 100 / capital-at-charge = 2,400 x 100 / 32,000 = 7.5 per cent.

q: Under the pre-merger financial convention, the dividend payable by a railway on a capital-at-charge (excluding the capital invested in strategic lines) of Rs 12,500 crore, at the rate of 4 per cent per annum, would amount to:
e: Dividend = 4 per cent of the capital-at-charge = 4 x 12,500 / 100 = Rs 500 crore.

q: The total expenditure of the Government of India for a year is Rs 38,00,000 crore, its revenue receipts are Rs 25,00,000 crore and its non-debt capital receipts are Rs 2,00,000 crore. The fiscal deficit of the Government for the year is:
e: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure - (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts) = 38,00,000 - (25,00,000 + 2,00,000) = Rs 11,00,000 crore.

q: The fiscal deficit of the Government of India for a year is Rs 8,40,000 crore and the interest payments during the year are Rs 5,60,000 crore. The primary deficit of the Government for the year is:
e: Primary deficit = fiscal deficit - interest payments = 8,40,000 - 5,60,000 = Rs 2,80,000 crore.

q: The revenue deficit of the Government of India for a year is Rs 4,60,000 crore and the grants given to the States and others for the creation of capital assets during the year are Rs 1,85,000 crore. The effective revenue deficit of the Government for the year is:
e: Effective revenue deficit = revenue deficit - grants for creation of capital assets = 4,60,000 - 1,85,000 = Rs 2,75,000 crore.

q: Article 272 of the Constitution, which dealt with taxes levied and collected by the Union and distributed between the Union and the States, was omitted by:
e: Article 272 of the Constitution, which dealt with taxes levied and collected by the Union and distributed between the Union and the States, was omitted by the Constitution (Eightieth Amendment) Act, 2000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A cess levied for specific purposes forms part of the divisible pool of taxes shareable with the States under Article 270 of the Constitution.
2. A surcharge levied under Article 271 of the Constitution is excluded from the divisible pool shareable with the States.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false, as a cess levied for specific purposes is excluded from the divisible pool under Article 270; statement 2 is true, since a surcharge levied under Article 271 is likewise excluded from the divisible pool shareable with the States.

q: Which of the following correctly states the position regarding the salaries and pensions of the Judges of a High Court?

options.A: Both the salaries and the pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Both the salaries and the pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State
options.C: The salaries and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State, while the pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: The salaries and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, while the pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State

e: The salaries and allowances of the Judges of a High Court are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State, while their pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Proclamation of Financial Emergency issued under Article 360 of the Constitution shall cease to operate at the expiration of two months unless it is approved by resolutions of both Houses of Parliament before the expiration of that period.
2. During a Financial Emergency, the President may issue directions for the reduction of the salaries of persons serving in connection with the affairs of the Union, including the Judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: a Financial Emergency proclamation ceases after two months unless approved by both Houses of Parliament, and during it the President may direct reduction of salaries, including those of Supreme Court and High Court Judges.

q: Under Article 148 of the Constitution, after the Comptroller and Auditor General of India ceases to hold office, he:

options.A: Is not eligible for any further office under the Government of India or under the Government of any State
options.B: Is eligible for appointment as the Governor of a State
options.C: Is eligible for further office after a cooling-off period of two years
options.D: Is eligible for further office with the approval of the President

e: Under Article 148, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, after he ceases to hold office, is not eligible for any further office under the Government of India or under the Government of any State.

q: Under the framework of the International Standards of Supreme Audit Institutions (ISSAI), ISSAI 200 sets out the fundamental principles of:
e: Under the ISSAI framework, ISSAI 200 sets out the fundamental principles of financial auditing.

q: 'Social audit', as distinct from the audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, is carried out by:

options.A: The internal audit wing of the department concerned
options.B: A firm of chartered accountants engaged by the department
options.C: The Accountant General of the State concerned
options.D: The beneficiaries and the community themselves, such as the Gram Sabha under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act

e: Social audit is carried out by the beneficiaries and the community themselves, such as the Gram Sabha under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, and not by the CAG or departmental auditors.

q: The creation of an independent Fiscal Council, to advise on fiscal matters and to assess the fiscal performance of the Government, was recommended by:
e: The creation of an independent Fiscal Council, to advise on fiscal matters and assess the fiscal performance of the Government, was recommended by the FRBM Review Committee.

q: The market borrowings (public debt) of the State Governments in India are also managed by:
e: The market borrowings of the State Governments in India are also managed by the Reserve Bank of India, which conducts their loan flotations.

q: State Development Loans, through which the State Governments raise their market borrowings, are:

options.A: Treasury Bills issued by the State Governments
options.B: Short-term loans advanced by the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: Bonds issued by the public sector undertakings of the States
options.D: Dated securities issued by the State Governments through the Reserve Bank of India

e: State Development Loans, through which State Governments raise their market borrowings, are dated securities issued by the State Governments through the Reserve Bank of India.

q: The Reserve Bank of India transacts the general banking business of a State Government, as its agent, under agreements entered into with that Government under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, namely:
e: The Reserve Bank of India transacts the general banking business of a State Government, as its agent, under agreements entered into under Section 21A of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

q: The Fourteenth Finance Commission recommended that the share of the States in the net proceeds of the divisible pool of central taxes should be raised to:
e: The Fourteenth Finance Commission recommended that the share of the States in the net proceeds of the divisible pool of central taxes should be raised to 42 per cent.

q: In the horizontal devolution of the divisible pool of central taxes among the States recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission, the weight assigned to the criterion of 'tax and fiscal efforts' is:
e: In the Fifteenth Finance Commission's horizontal devolution criteria, the criterion of tax and fiscal efforts carried a weight of 2.5 per cent.

q: Under the Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act, 2017, the compensation payable to a State is computed by projecting the growth of its revenue over the base year 2015-16 at the rate of:
e: Under the GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017, compensation to a State is computed by projecting the growth of its revenue over the base year 2015-16 at the rate of 14 per cent per annum.

q: As held by the Supreme Court in the Mohit Minerals case, the recommendations of the Goods and Services Tax Council are:

options.A: Binding on the Union but not on the States
options.B: Not binding on the Union or on the States, though they have persuasive value
options.C: Binding on both the Union and the States
options.D: Binding only after they are notified by the Union Government

e: In the Mohit Minerals case, the Supreme Court held that the recommendations of the GST Council are not binding on the Union or on the States, though they have persuasive value.

q: Under Article 366(12A) of the Constitution, the expression 'goods and services tax' means a tax on the supply of goods or services or both, other than taxes on the supply of:
e: Under Article 366(12A), 'goods and services tax' means a tax on the supply of goods or services or both, other than taxes on the supply of alcoholic liquor for human consumption.

q: Under Article 286 of the Constitution, no law of a State shall impose a tax on the supply of goods or services where such supply takes place:

options.B: In the course of inter-State trade or commerce
options.C: At the first point of sale within the State
options.D: Outside the State, or in the course of the import of the goods or services into, or export of the goods or services out of, the territory of India

e: Under Article 286, no State law shall impose a tax on the supply of goods or services where the supply takes place outside the State, or in the course of import into, or export out of, the territory of India.

q: Under Article 287 of the Constitution, no law of a State shall impose a tax on the consumption or sale of electricity which is consumed by, or is sold for consumption to:

options.A: The departments of the State Government
options.B: The municipal corporations and other local bodies
options.C: The Government of India, including consumption in the construction, maintenance or working of a railway
options.D: The public sector undertakings of the Union

e: Under Article 287, no State law shall impose a tax on electricity consumed by the Government of India, or sold for consumption to it, including its consumption in the construction, maintenance or working of a railway.

q: Under Article 276 of the Constitution, the total amount payable by any one person in a year by way of taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments shall not exceed:
e: Under Article 276, the total amount payable by any one person in a year by way of taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments shall not exceed Rs 2,500.

q: 'Railways' is a subject enumerated in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution under:
e: 'Railways' is enumerated in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule under Entry 22, giving Parliament exclusive power to legislate on it.

q: The Rail Development Authority, an independent body set up to advise the Government on, among other things, the pricing of railway services and the raising of non-fare revenues, was set up in the year:
e: The Rail Development Authority, an independent body advising the Government on pricing of railway services and raising of non-fare revenues among other things, was set up in the year 2017.

q: In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account of the Government, the transactions relating to the Contingency Fund of India are accounted for under Major Head:
e: In the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, the transactions relating to the Contingency Fund of India are accounted for under Major Head 8000.

q: The 'golden rule' of public finance requires that the borrowings of the Government should be used:

options.A: Only for the creation of capital assets, the revenue account being balanced or in surplus
options.B: For meeting the revenue deficit of the Government
options.C: For the repayment of the loans raised earlier
options.D: For meeting any expenditure incurred in excess of the Budget provision

e: The 'golden rule' of public finance requires that Government borrowings be used only for the creation of capital assets, the revenue account being balanced or in surplus.

q: In public finance, the term 'fiscal marksmanship' refers to:

options.A: The level of the fiscal deficit of the Government
options.B: The speed with which the budgetary provisions are spent
options.C: The accuracy of the budget estimates of the Government when compared with the actual figures
options.D: The quality of the debt portfolio of the Government

e: 'Fiscal marksmanship' refers to the accuracy of the budget estimates of the Government when compared with the actual figures; good marksmanship means the estimates prove close to the outcomes.

q: The guarantees given by the Government in respect of loans raised by public sector undertakings and other bodies are treated in the Government accounts as:

options.A: A part of the outstanding public debt of the Government
options.B: Revenue expenditure of the year in which they are given
options.D: Contingent liabilities, which become actual liabilities only when they are invoked or devolve on the Government

e: Guarantees given by the Government for loans raised by public sector undertakings and other bodies are contingent liabilities, which become actual liabilities only when they are invoked or devolve on the Government.

q: In respect of the expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, the position under the Constitution is that such expenditure:

options.A: Is submitted to the vote of Parliament but is not discussed by it
options.B: Is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, but nothing in the Constitution prevents a discussion of it in either House
options.C: Is neither submitted to the vote of Parliament nor discussed by it
options.D: Is submitted to the vote of the Rajya Sabha only

e: Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, but nothing in the Constitution prevents a discussion of it in either House.

q: The proposals contained in the Finance Bill for the levy or increase of customs and excise duties take effect immediately from the date of the introduction of the Bill, by virtue of a declaration made under:

options.A: The Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931
options.B: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003
options.C: The Finance Act of the previous year

e: The proposals in the Finance Bill for levy or increase of customs and excise duties take effect immediately from the date of introduction of the Bill, by virtue of a declaration made under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931.

q: The FRBM Review Committee recommended that the debt of each State Government should be contained within a ceiling of:

options.A: 3 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product
options.B: 10 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product
options.C: 20 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product
options.D: 40 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product

e: The FRBM Review Committee recommended that the debt of each State Government should be contained within a ceiling of 20 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product.

q: Under the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, one of the members of the Finance Commission shall be a person who:

options.A: Is a serving Judge of the Supreme Court
options.C: Is the Comptroller and Auditor General of India for the time being
options.D: Is, or has been, or is qualified to be, a Judge of a High Court

e: Under the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, one of the members of the Finance Commission shall be a person who is, or has been, or is qualified to be, a Judge of a High Court.

q: Performance budgeting was introduced in the Government of India following the recommendations of:
e: Performance budgeting was introduced in the Government of India following the recommendations of the First Administrative Reforms Commission.
